explanations: There is none. The clock is injected and fixed per test, so the cutoff tests are deterministic. The in-memory repo copies on seed, get and save, so the test cannot pass by mutating a shared object the dispatcher also holds; the 'already dispatched' test genuinely reads back what was saved. Each test builds fresh fakes via setup(), so no state leaks between tests, and the RecordingCarrier asserts on real call counts and arguments rather than on a stubbed return alone.

A real repository returns fresh objects. If the fake returned the stored reference, mutating the object would look 'persisted' even without save. Copying keeps the fake faithful. It is not about speed, typing, or the carrier, which never sees the repo.
The check is getUTCHours() >= cutoffHourUtc, so 17:00 counts as past cutoff; setUTCDate(+1) on March 31 yields April 1. UTC getters are used, not local time, and the carrier fake does no validation.

The FixedClock only helps if the code under test reads time through it. Bypassing it ties the result to wall-clock time, making the tests time-dependent. It would still compile, and pickup date is derived from the current time, not from shipment data.
